questions.question: If a storeroom of a house is in the shape of a cuboid having a length of 3 m, a width of 2 m, and a height of 4 m, find the total area of its four walls.

length of 3 m, width of 2 m, and height of 4 m.

Area of 4 walls = 2(l + b)h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of 4 walls = 2(l + b)h

⇒ Area of 4 walls = 2(3 + 2)4 = 40

Thus, Heights are in inches: 78 inch, 72 inch, 68 inch, 74 inch, 76 inch, 70 inch

Average = 438 / 6 = 73 inches 

⇒ 6 feet 1 inch

questions.question: In a bag there are coins of ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10 denominations. The total number of coins in the bag is 300 . If the number of coins of ₹2 , ₹5 and ₹10 denominations are in the ratio of 1 ∶ 2 ∶ 3, then what is the total amount of money in the bag?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let, the number of ₹2, ₹5, and ₹10 denominations in the bag are x, 2x, and 3x.

Given, The Total number of coins is 300.

Hence,

⇒ x + 2x + 3x = 300 

⇒ x = 50

So the number of coins of ₹2, ₹5, and ₹10 denominations are 50, 100, and 150.

The total amount will be given by:

⇒ 2100

questions.question: If the circumference of a circle is equal to the perimeter of a square, and the radius of the given circle is positive, then which of the following options is correct?

options.text: Area of the circle > Area of the square
Area of the circle ≥ Area of the square
Area of the circle = Area of the square

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2D figures having the exact same given perimeter, the figure with the greater number of sides encloses a larger area.

A circle can be considered a regular polygon with an infinite number of sides.

Thus, a circle always encloses the maximum possible area for a fixed perimeter compared to any other polygon.

Since the square and the circle have equal perimeters, the circle will enclose the greater area.

**∴ The correct answer is Area of the circle > Area of the square.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the radius of the given circle be r and the side of the square be a.

 
 
• 
 r
 
 Area = π × r²
 Circumference = 2πr
 
 
 a
 Area = a²
 Perimeter = 4a
 
 

 Equal

⇒ Circumference of the circle = 2 × π × r

⇒ Perimeter of the square = 4 × a

⇒ Given that circumference is equal to perimeter: 2 × π × r = 4 × a

⇒ Side of the square (a) = (2 × π × r) ÷ 4 = (π × r) ÷ 2

⇒ Area of the circle (A꜀) = π × r²

⇒ Area of the square (Aₛ) = a² = [(π × r) ÷ 2]² = (π² × r²) ÷ 4

⇒ Ratio of their areas (A꜀ ÷ Aₛ) = (π × r²) ÷ [(π² × r²) ÷ 4]

⇒ A꜀ ÷ Aₛ = 4 ÷ π

⇒ Since π ≈ 3.14, the value of 4 ÷ 3.14 is greater than 1.

⇒ Therefore, A꜀ > Aₛ (Since r is positive, area cannot be zero).

**∴ The correct answer is Area of the circle > Area of the square.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isoperimetric Inequality

For any closed curve of a given fixed perimeter, the circle is the unique shape that encloses the maximum possible area.

Regular Polygons with Same Perimeter

If different regular polygons have the exact same perimeter, the polygon with the greater number of sides always has a larger area (e.g., Equilateral Triangle < Square < Regular Pentagon < Regular Hexagon).

Shapes with Same Area

Conversely, if a circle and any regular polygon have the same given area, the circle will always have the minimum possible perimeter.

questions.question: A man rows from J to K (upstream) and back from K to J (downstream) in a total time of 15 hours. The distance between J and K is 300 km. The time taken by the man to row 9 km downstream is identical to the time taken by him to row 3 km upstream. What is the approximate speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A man rows from J to K (upstream) and back from K to J (downstream) in a total time of 15 hours.

The distance between J and K is 300 km.

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

Let us assume that the speed of boat in still water is B and speed of stream is S.

A man rows from J to K (upstream) and back from K to J (downstream) in a total time of 15 hours. The distance between J and K is 300 km.

⇒ (300)/(B + C) + (300)/(B - C) = 15

⇒ (20)/(B + C) + (20)/(B - C) = 1 .................(I)

The time taken by the man to row 9 km downstream is identical to the time taken by him to row 3 km upstream.

⇒ (9)/(B + C) = (3)/(B - C)

⇒ (B + C)/(B - C) = (3)/(1)

Apply Componendo and Dividendo Rule;

⇒ (B)/(C) = (2)/(1)

∴ Speed of boat in still water, B = 2x km/h, and

Speed of stream, S = x km/h

Put these values in equation(i),

⇒ (20)/(2x + x) + (20)/(2x - x) = 1

⇒ (20)/(3x) + (20)/(x) = 1

⇒ 20 + 60 = 3x

⇒ x = 80/3

∴ Speed of boat in still water, B = 2x km/h = 2 × 80/3

⇒ 160/3 = 53.33 km/h

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: There is a profit of 10% when an item is sold at (5)/(6) of its actual selling price. What will be the profit percentage on the cost price when the item is sold at its actual selling price?
questions.solution:
Given:

By selling an article at (5)/(6) of selling price, a trader incurred a profit of 10%.

Formula Used:

Profit% = (selling price - cost price)/cost price × 100

Calculation:

Let the cost price of that article be Rs. 100x

Selling price when sold at (5)/(6) of original selling price = 100x + 100x × 10%

⇒ 110x

Original selling price = 110x × (6)/(5) = 132x

Required profit % = [(132x - 100x)/100x] × 100

⇒ 32%

∴ The profit percentage on selling it at its actual selling price is 32%.
